cap10_start: mid PHYS 396 CAPUT DECIMUM / Resurrectionem ... demonstratur e Veteri Testamento
titles: CHAPTER NINE. The resurrection of the dead is proved possible from natural principles; five heads follow
II. Future resurrection not demonstrable by nature's light; possibility and fittingness can be proved (Scotus)
Aphorism's two members; prior reason is God's free will; posterior reasons ad hominem or ad rem
Ad hominem: fathers press pagans with their own revivification stories — Theophilus, Aeneas, Pliny
RATIO I. From the soul's natural union with the body; immortality seems to demand reunion (Thomas)
II. From natural desire for felicity; incomplete happiness without the body (Thomas)
Gentile reply on desire; III. From divine justice — reward and punishment for soul and body (Thomas, Tertullian)
IV–V. Actions and passions are of the whole person; reason persuades but does not compel
Nature and art types of reunion: Nyssen's quicksilver; potter, glass, chemistry — Cap. 9 close
